title: HiResMet2: (HighResection in brain metastases): R0 resection alone vs. gross-total resection with postoperative radiotherapy for non-eloquent, supratentorial brain metastases – A Proof-of-Concept-Study
summary:
Background
In the surgery of brain metastases, the resection margin has so far been determined intraoperatively based on imaging (MRI), without histological control of the margins — unlike the standard established in other surgical disciplines. This established form of resection, with histologically confirmed tumor-free margins, is referred to in other surgical disciplines as R0 resection. R0 resection has not previously been investigated in neurosurgery, even though it is known that tumor cells infiltrate beyond the MRI-visible tumor border into the surrounding brain tissue in approximately 50% of cases (Berghoff et al., 2013). The indication for subsequent irradiation of the tumor bed is based on the assumption of residual tumor cells in the surrounding tissue.

Studies suggest that a more extensive resection of the surrounding tissue can improve tumor control: following complete tumor resection with subsequent irradiation, recurrences occur at a similar rate to that seen after a histologically confirmed complete ("R0") resection without any irradiation at all (Yoo et al., 2009). To date, a standardized surgical concept for such a cellularly complete resection is lacking in brain metastasis surgery.

In our pilot study (HiResMet1), such an R0 resection (followed by irradiation) was safely feasible for metastases located non-eloquent brain regions and was associated with a low recurrence rate (4% at 6.5 months). For comparison, recurrence rates reported in the literature after conventional resection are 46–57% without irradiation and 10–28% with irradiation (each at 12 months).

In addition, recent evidence suggests that irradiation, through effects on the immune system, may promote the growth of metastases at other sites in the body (Piffkó et al., 2025). Forgoing irradiation when complete resection has been confirmed could counteract this effect and also reduce treatment burden: fewer treatment appointments, fewer radiation-related side effects (e.g., edema, radiation necrosis, cognitive impairment), and a possible improvement in quality of life.

Research question
HiResMet 2 is a randomized proof-of-concept study. It aims to evaluate the efficacy of this novel surgical concept and, for the first time, to prospectively test whether resection alone — achieving cellularly complete tumor removal without subsequent irradiation — is equivalent to standard treatment (complete resection plus irradiation) with respect to local tumor control within 12 months.

Study procedure
In the intervention arm, an R0 resection is targeted, and subsequent irradiation is omitted. In the control arm, no R0 resection is performed; instead, a conventional resection is carried out, without a safety margin and without histological control of the resection margins for tumor cells. In the control arm, postoperative irradiation is then performed according to clinical routine. The two groups are compared with respect to recurrence rates.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Radiological suspicion of one or more brain metastases in a patient with a known primary tumor or cancer of unknown primary (CUP)
- Indication for resection of one or more brain metastases
- Non-eloquent tumor location: distance of at least 2 cm from the motor cortex, visual cortex, and frontal operculum
- KPS ≥ 70%
Exclusion criteria:
Cerebellar location
Eloquent location: eloquent is defined as the motor cortex and the frontal operculum, depending on the patient's handedness
KPS ≤ 70%
Preoperative irradiation (stereotactic radiotherapy or whole-brain radiotherapy)
Postoperative whole-brain radiotherapy
